source: JPL Horizons DE441; ICRF vectors; lunar MEAN_ME high-precision site orientation
vector_construction: At lunar reflection epoch t (mid exposure minus Moon-to-HST downleg), e=Earth(t-LT_E)-site and s=Sun(t-LT_S)-site from the sampled selenographic site; rho=|e x u|, D=e.u, S=|s-e| for sunward u=(s-e)/|s-e|. Site vectors originate at the lunar surface point, so receiver-side (HST) parallax is exact and not an uncertainty term; the downleg only shifts the epoch (Moon-HST range/c, ~1.28 s). Site states come from the Horizons OBSERVER pipeline (astrometric ICRF direction times delta distance; the VECTORS pipeline served time-only rows at retrieval time, including for the previously validated December-2011 request shape), which matches the December 2011 LT convention of applying no apparent-sky stellar aberration.
horizons_hst_probe: Moon vectors from HST (-48) confirmed available (DE441); A5 assumption verified. HST position enters only the downleg shift: a geocentric fallback would change the shift by <=6911 km/c = 0.023 s (~40 km sampled displacement), not the shadow geometry.
longitude_convention: Table 1 selenographic longitudes read east-positive (IAU/SPICE modern convention, same as Horizons Moon site coordinates); validated by the RA_APER pointing check below.

epoch_contract.reflection_epoch_shift: mid exposure time minus Moon-to-HST downleg; downleg interpolated linearly from 1-minute Moon-from-HST DE441 ranges
epoch_contract.site_vector_sampling: Earth/Sun vectors from each selenographic site linearly interpolated at the reflection epoch between 1-minute Horizons samples (Horizons rejects sub-minute steps); interpolation error <~2 km, far below the 150 km probe scale

spatial_sensitivity.probe_semantics: Sampled point displaced +/-150 km toward/away from the shadow axis on the lunar surface (rho +/- 150 km), mirroring the December 2011 radial probe scale.
spatial_sensitivity.pointing_terms_source: Youngblood et al. 2020 Sec. II.1: 14" initial gyro slew, gyro guiding accumulating at 0.001"/s (16.48" max orbit 2, 10.72" max orbit 3), linear-track approximation dominating at up to 10 arcmin.
spatial_sensitivity.scope: Displacement sensitivity, not a confidence interval; the track-error envelope exceeds the 150 km probe and limits the same-region albedo cancellation premise, see limitations.

mid_time_fits_vs_table1.scope: TIME-OBS is the first CR-SPLIT member (or single-exposure) start and mid = TIME-OBS + member exposure/2; later CR-SPLIT members take their Table-1 mid-time offsets from the first member, so their diffs are constructed from Table 1 rather than independently checked - only the four first members and the twelve single exposures carry independent FITS evidence

eclipse_angle_table1_vs_horizons.scope: Table 1 evaluates e at the fixed selenographic (0,0) site at observed mid times; Horizons site vectors reproduce the same angle definition.

pointing_ra_aper_vs_table1.scope: Body frame reconstructed from Horizons sub-observer longitude/latitude and pole direction (no hand-coded east/west sign); residuals judged only for single-exposure sets and first CR-SPLIT members, the only commanded pointings recorded in the headers. Residual scatter is the paper's documented linear-track approximation error; the east-positive Table 1 convention is confirmed by residuals far inside that budget.

limitations: Sampled positions are the paper's published mean linear-track coordinates; the actual in-exposure pointing wanders within the documented error budget (up to 10 arcmin track approximation error), so the in/out sampled lunar regions can differ and albedo cancellation is conditional on the nominal pointing record.

The Lommel-Seeliger per-exposure correction applied by the paper (F_LS in 0.4975-0.5021, incidence/emission angles closely coupled) changes ratios by <=1% and is omitted here; the paper's penumbral limb-darkening division (G430L I/I0 0.7-0.79) is likewise not reproduced for the auxiliary penumbral branch.
Selenographic (0,0) eclipse-angle check absorbs SPICE-vs-MEAN_ME orientation differences within 0.1 deg; per-exposure eclipse angles from Table 1 are evaluated at (0,0), not at the sampled point.
